en: CUL Or. 155:

This manuscript contains various *Cakrasaṃvara* texts by one Chātrakumāradatta, described as a *paramopāsaka*, along with another work following the tradition of Lūyīpāda (the name is spelled consistently throughout). He identifies his guru as "the one residing in Kanyārāma. Kanyārāma is depicted on fol. 127r of CUL Add. [1643].

In 1643 [CE], he resided at a seat of Lokanātha in Rāḍhā, now in West Bengal. The toponym is given as a synonym for Lokeśvara in Puruṣottama’s *Trikāṇḍaśeṣa*, verse 1.1.15cd (ca. 1100–1150 CE). Another guru mentioned is possibly Sauṣṭhavapāda, who was styled *mahāmaṇḍalācārya*.
The person requesting at least one of the works is identified (if my emendation is correct) as Nandadāsa.
[In a much later hand: The Sādhana of Cakrasaṃvara. [1v] Siddham. Oṃ. Homage to Vajraḍāka!

Śrī Cakrasaṃvara-Vajravārāhī; Ḍākinī; Lāmā; Khaṇḍarohā; Rūpiṇī; Khaṇḍakapālī; Pracaṇḍā; Mahākaṅkāla; Caṇḍākṣī; Kaṅkālaprabhāvatī; Vikaṭadaṃṣṭriṇī-Mahānāsā; Surāvairiṇī-Vīramatī; Amitābha-Kharparī; Vajraprabhā-Laṅkeśvarī; Vajradeha-Drumacchāyā; Aṅkurikā-Airāvatī; Vajrajaṭilā-Mahābhairavā; Mahāvīrā-Vāyuvegā; Vajrahūṃkārā-Surābhakṣī.

Subhadraśyāmādevī; Vajrabhadrasubhadrā; Mahābhairavahayakarṇā; Virūpākṣakhagānanā; Mahābalacakravegā; Raktavajrakhaṇḍarohā; Hayagrīvaśauṇḍinī; Ākāśagarbhacakravarmiṇī; Śrīherukasuvīrā; Padmanarteśvaramahābalā; Vairocanacakravartinī; Vajrasattvamahāvīryā; Kākāsyā; Ulukāsyā; Śvānāsyā; Sūkarāsyā; Yamadāḍhī; Yamadūtī; Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī.
Yamamathanī. Thus concludes the explanation of the names of the Heroes and Heroines in the *Cakrasaṃvara* according to the *Sādhana* of Luipāda.
Having prostrated before that Great Hero, who is joined with great passion, beautiful with innate bliss, and whose meditation proceeds from stage to higher stage;
The unsurpassed ritual of worship, as received through oral instruction by the student Kumāradatta,
is here written down according to the sequence of the *Saṃvara*.
The yogi should constantly worship the assembly of heroes and yoginīs in the directions starting from the east with the left hand, and in the order beginning from the southeast with the right hand.
The yogin should constantly worship with these mantras: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ. He should offer water for bathing, purification with flowers, and cow-dung water. [Then follows] the *Sumbhādi*...
[perhaps one folio is missing].
Oṃ ye hūṃ 3 phaṭ | Oṃ yamadaṃṣṭriṇīye hūṃ 3 phaṭ | Oṃ yamamathanīye hūṃ 3 phaṭ || [The goddesses] beginning with the Gatekeepers. 8 ||

Having performed the recitation, praise, taking refuge in the Three Jewels, and the dedication of merit through aspiration, one should request forgiveness: *muḥ*. This is the ritual for worship in the *Śrī Cakrasaṃvara* according to the *Sādhana* of Luipāda.

The outer-secret mental worship; the cultivation of the four divine abodes, beginning with loving-kindness; the purification of the deities within the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements; the protection wheel; emptiness; the accomplishment of the seed-syllables and deities of the exterior and so forth; the summoning of the wisdom-being (*jñānasattva*); the armor; the consecration of body, speech, and mind; the purification of the Noble Lady (*Bhaṭṭārikā*); the purification of the vajra and lotus; the empowerment (*abhiṣeka*); the nourishment with nectar (*amṛta*); the placement of the hand-gestures (*mudrā*); the instruction; the recitation of mantra; and the offering (*bali*). 17.
Homage to Śrī Cakrasaṃvara!
I pay homage to Śrī Cakrasaṃvara, who manifests the three bodies— the Dharma, Enjoyment, and Emanation— and who abides in the thirty-seven yogas.
I bow with my whole being to the one who dwells in Kanyārāma, by whose grace my mind is fixed upon the Supreme Self amidst all moving things.
And that great ocean of the *sādhana* of the glorious Saṃvara,
which was composed by Luipāda in both direct and reverse order, must be understood.
Having understood many tantras that have emerged from the secret vagina,
[I shall explain] that which was taught by my gurus who dwell in the grove of maidens.
And by the great masters of the great mandala, those of noble conduct,
I shall string that together like jewels upon a thread.
And I was entreated with devotion by the wise Nandadāsa;
and an instruction was granted to me by my teacher, whose mind was joyful.
Even for another who is considered similar [to Luipāda] following this tradition of Luipāda’s lineage,
this [work], though intended for his own benefit, [is beneficial] to him according to the degrees of weak, middling, and intense.

For the sake of gathering the equipment of merit: from the syllable *Āḥ* arises a moon disc, upon which is the syllable *Hūṃ*. One performs the outer, secret, and mental offerings; and having performed the three refuges and so forth, [one recites] *Muḥ*.
For the sake of bringing the paths of the Śrāvakas and others to cessation: one cultivates the four divine abodes (*brahmavihāra*), namely, loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity.

For the purpose of purifying the ordinary aggregates (*skandha*): Vairocana is in the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*); Ratnasaṃbhava, the Vajra-Sun, is in sensation (*vedanā*); Padmanarteśvara is in perception (*saṃjñā*); Amitābha is in mental formations (*saṃskāra*); Vajrarāja is in consciousness (*vijñānaskandha*); and Amoghasiddhi is Vajrasattva. Akṣobhya is Śrī Herukavajra in the state of all Tathāgatas; [he is also] Vajrasattva. Mohavajrā is white in the eye; Dveṣavajrā is black in the two ears; Īrṣyāvajrā is dark green in the two nostrils.

In the mouth is Rāgavajrā, red; in touch is Mātsaryavajrā, yellow; in all the sense-bases (āyatana) is Aiśvaryavajrā, red or white. The earth element is Pātanī; Locanā is white as bone. The water element is Māraṇī; the goddess Māmakī is black. The fire element is Ākarṣaṇī; Pāṇḍarā is either pale-red or hot-red. The wind element is Narteśvarī; Tārā is dark blue. The space element is Padmajvālinī; she is very pure emptiness, red or white.
Thus is the purification of the deities within the aggregates (skandha), bases (āyatana), and elements (dhātu).

For the purpose of destroying the Māras of the aggregates (*skandha*) and so forth: *raṃ ravi*, *hūṃ* (the crossed-vajra). Again, situated in the center of the *vajraṭaka*: *ravi hūṃ*. With these mantras: *Oṃ sumbha nisumbha hūṃ 2 phaṭ* | *Oṃ gṛhṇa 2 huṃ 2 phaṭ* | *Oṃ gṛhṇāpaya 2 huṃ 2 phaṭ* | *Oṃ ānaya ho bhagavān vajrarāja hūṃ 2 phaṭ* | [One should visualize] the eight goddesses, then the sky-walker (*khecarī*), the earth-walker (*bhūcarī*), and the subterranean dweller (*pātālavāsinī*), and having constructed the vajra-fence (*vajraprākāra*) and so forth.

Oṃ gha gha ghātaya [the wicked] phaṭ! Kīlaya 2 all sins phaṭ! Hūṃ 3! O Vajrakīla, Vajradhara commands: O Vajrakīla of the body, speech, and mind of all obstructors, hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ vajramudgara, strike down the Vajrakīla, hūṃ phaṭ! Thus is the protection wheel for the purpose of abandoning views such as that of a self. Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by nature; I am pure by nature. Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the wisdom of emptiness. Thus is the twofold emptiness of the selflessness of phenomena and the selflessness of persons.

For the sake of attaining perfect enlightenment: Yaṃ is wind; Raṃ is fire; Vaṃ is water; Laṃ is earth; Suṃ is Sumeru; Hūṃ is the crossed-vajra (viśvavajra); Paṃ is the crossed-lotus (viśvapadma). Above the moon-maṇḍala is the syllable Hūṃ, encircled by the vowels and consonants rotating counter-clockwise and clockwise. From this arises the complete maṇḍala-circle, beginning with the Lord [Vairocana]. Having summoned the Jñānasattva by means of light rays from the seed-syllable Hūṃ situated upon the moon in the heart, one recites: "Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through yoga; I am pure through yoga."

Thus is the unification of the Jñānasattva and the Samayasattva. Oṃ hā namaḥ hi | svāhā hūṃ | vauṣaṭ he | huṃ huṃ ho | phaṭ haṃ | oṃ vaṃ | hāṃ yoṃ | hrīṃ moṃ | pheṃ hrīṃ | huṃ huṃ phaṭ phaṭ | Thus is the double armor (*kavaca*). Oṃ āḥ hūṃ. Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-body, speech, and mind of all heroes and yoginīs. Oṃ, all phenomena are vajra-pure; I am vajra-pure. Thus is the consecration of body, speech, and mind.

Oṃ sarvabuddhaḍākinīye vajravarṇanīye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Thus is the purification of the Noble Lady (Bhaṭṭārikā). Vyādyā. This is the purification of the vajra and the lotus. Within the moon at the heart, by means of the rays from the seed-syllable HŪṂ: "Just as all the Tathāgatas were bathed immediately upon birth, so shall I bathe [you] with pure, divine water. Oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaśriye hūṃ. Thus is the consecration (abhiṣeka). Above the wind-maṇḍala is the fire-maṇḍala; a lotus vessel born from the syllable ĀḤ.

Above that is the seed-syllable of the Vīraśumā Tathāgatas: OṂ TRĪṂ JRĪṂ KHAṂ HŪṂ. Above the span (vitasti) is the syllable OṂ situated upon the moon. Having purified the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) with the three syllables, there is a white three-pronged vajra arising from the syllable HŪṂ on the tongue. Thus is the nourishment by nectar (*amṛtāpyāyana*). [The seed-syllables of] the Nirmāṇakāya: PU, JĀ, OṂ, A, GO, RĀ, HE, MĀ, KĀ, O, TRI, KO, KA, LA, KĀ, HI, PRE, GṚ, SAU, SU, NA, ŚI, MA, KU.

Thus is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the regions, such as Pullīramalaya and others, upon the head and other parts of the body; this is the Saṃbhogakāya. A certain sequence for the meditation on the instructions for the means of accomplishment (*sādhanopadeśabhāvanā*) is the Vāpaṭitreli-krama. The Dharmakāya consists of the recitation (*japa*) of the root mantra and other mantras. Having prepared the sacrificial offering (*bali*) according to the sequence of the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*), [one recites]: *HŪṂ PHAṂ* situated upon the moon; with the flame-gesture (*jvālāmudrā*): *OṂ ĀRALLI HOḤ HAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOṂ (HOḤ) VAJRAḌĀKINYAḤ SAMAYASTHAṂ DṚŚYA HOḤ*.

Having recited [the name] three times and addressed them, [one performs] the heart-seal (*hṛdayamudrā*). Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi! May all *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *bhūtas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, *unmādas*, *apasmāras*, *ḍākinīs*, and so forth, accept this *bali* offering; protect the pledge (*samaya*); bestow all accomplishments (*siddhi*); eat and drink as you wish and according to your pleasure; do not transgress; be my companions for the sake of purifying the true happiness in every way. Hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā. This is the *bali* mantra.
The supreme lay devotee Chhātrakumāradatta, for his own remembrance,
has with great effort performed this meritorious work through the grace of his teacher’s command.
And all the yoginīs, heroes, and those born of heroes will forgive me whatever has been said or left unsaid; all that is established in the *sādhana*.

This is the *Śrīcakrasaṃvara-lūyīpādīya-sādhanopadeśa-bhāvanā-yathānukrama-ṭīpaṇaka*. Homage to Saṃvara! First, the yogin enters while seated upon a comfortable cushion. [This text was likely copied in the wrong place; it follows: It was written by Chhatra Kumāradatta for the benefit of sentient beings. Om.

Homage to Vajraḍāka! On the eastern petal is Rūpikā; on the northern petal, Cumbikā; on the western petal, Lāmā; on the southern petal, Parāvṛtā. (4) On the northeastern petal is Savālikā; on the northwestern petal, Avartikā; on the southwestern petal, Aihikī; on the southeastern petal, Ḍākinī. (4) These goddesses are blue in color and four-armed. They stand in the *ālīḍha* posture and have one face. With their two left hands, they hold a heart, a raised index finger (*tarjanī*), and a *khaṭvāṅga*.

Holding a vajra and a skull-cup with their two right hands, wearing garlands of skulls and strings of severed heads, and having heads adorned with a universal vajra, a moon, and a skull-cup; in the heart is the Knowledge Being (jñānasattva), likewise surrounded by eight goddesses situated upon a universal lotus and sun.
